'''Adachi Yoshikage''' (安達 義景) was a mid-{{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} military commander and the heir of {{ill|Adachi Kagemori|en|Adachi Kagemori|qid=Q2823876|lt=Adachi Kagemori}}.<ref>Ueda Masaki, Tsuda Hideo, Nagahara Keiji, Fujii Shōichi, Fujiwara Akira, "Concise Japanese Biographical Dictionary," 5th edition, Sanseidō, 2009, p. 41.</ref> He was a prominent {{ill|Gokenin|en|Gokenin|qid=Q63765|lt=Gokenin}} of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|qid=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate}} and the father of {{ill|Adachi Yasumori|ja|安達泰盛|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11133367}} and {{ill|Kakusan-ni|en|Kakusan-ni|qid=Q11630322|lt=Kakuzan-ni}}, who became the consort of {{ill|Hōjō Tokimune|en|Hōjō Tokimune|qid=Q430964|lt=Hōjō Tokimune}}.
== Biography ==
The character "義" in Yoshikage's name is thought to have been granted to him in {{ill|Gennin|en|Gennin|qid=Q1194430|lt=Gennin}} (1224) upon the death of {{ill|Hōjō Yoshitoki|en|Hōjō Yoshitoki|qid=Q1028811|lt=Hōjō Yoshitoki}}, the second {{ill|Shikken|en|Shikken|qid=Q1045904|lt=Shikken}} of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|en|Kamakura shogunate|qid=Q736839|lt=Kamakura shogunate}}. It is likely Yoshikage underwent his {{ill|Genpuku|ja|元服|comment=changed title based on wikidata|comment=enwiki is a redirect|qid=Q138321}} (coming-of-age ceremony) during Yoshitoki's later years.<ref>Fukushima Kaneharu, "Adachi Yasumori and the Kamakura Shogunate - The Shimotsuki Incident and Surrounding Events," Yūrin Shinsho, 2006, p. 40; Suzuki Hiromi, "The Adachi Clan," in "The Era of Hōjō Tokimune" (Yagi Bookstore, 2008), p. 330.</ref> After Yoshitoki's death, Yoshikage supported successive {{ill|Shikken|en|Shikken|qid=Q1045904|lt=Shikken}} from {{ill|Hōjō Yasutoki|en|Hōjō Yasutoki|qid=Q1188359|lt=Hōjō Yasutoki}} to {{ill|Hōjō Tokiyori|en|Hōjō Tokiyori|qid=Q1354410|lt=Hōjō Tokiyori}}. He served as one of the {{ill|Hyōjōshū|ca|Hyōjōshū|es|Hyōjōshū|fa|هیوجوشو|ja|評定衆|ko|효조슈|zh|評定眾|qid=Q11288036}} and was highly valued by the {{ill|Hōjō clan|en|Hōjō clan|qid=Q834364|lt=Hōjō clan}}.
As a {{ill|Hatamoto|en|Hatamoto|qid=Q572662|lt=Hatamoto}} of the shogunate, Yoshikage inherited the position of {{ill|Akita Jōsuke|ja|秋田城介|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11595284}} at the age of 29. In {{ill|Ninji|en|Ninji|qid=Q1194262|lt=Ninji}} 3 (1242), under orders from {{ill|Hōjō Yasutoki|en|Hōjō Yasutoki|qid=Q1188359|lt=Hōjō Yasutoki}}, he led efforts to enthrone {{ill|Emperor Go-Saga|en|Emperor Go-Saga|qid=Q349259|lt=Emperor Go-Saga}}. Yoshikage played a key role in the {{ill|Miya Uprising|ja|宮騒動|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11455334}} of [[Kangen]]{{efn|February 1243 to February 1247|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} 4 (1246), helping {{ill|Hōjō Tokiyori|en|Hōjō Tokiyori|qid=Q1354410|lt=Hōjō Tokiyori}} oust anti-{{ill|Tokusō|en|Tokusō|qid=Q1759237|lt=Tokusō}} factions like {{ill|Hōjō Mitsutoki|ja|北条光時|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11402082}}.
The power struggle between the {{ill|Hōjō clan|en|Hōjō clan|qid=Q834364|lt=Hōjō clan}} and the {{ill|Miura clan|en|Miura clan|qid=Q2053762|lt=Miura clan}} during this period also reflected Yoshikage's rivalry with {{ill|Miura Yasumura|ja|三浦泰村|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11356483}} for influence. In {{ill|Hōji (era)|en|Hōji (era)|qid=Q1327400|lt=Hōji}} 元年 (1247), Yoshikage, alongside his eldest son {{ill|Adachi Yasumori|ja|安達泰盛|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11133367}}, led forces to suppress the {{ill|Miura clan|en|Miura clan|qid=Q2053762|lt=Miura clan}} in the {{ill|Battle of Hōji|ja|宝治合戦|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11452590}}.
Yoshikage maintained a high-Ranking position under Tokiyori's {{ill|Tokusō system|ja|得宗専制体制|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135501969}}, and Tokiyori's son, {{ill|Hōjō Tokimune|en|Hōjō Tokimune|qid=Q430964|lt=Hōjō Tokimune}}, was born in the residence of Yoshikage's sister, {{ill|Matsushita-zenni|fa|ماتسوشیتازننی|ja|松下禅尼|ko|마쓰시타젠니|no|Matsushita Zenni|qid=Q11528974}}. Yoshikage's daughter, {{ill|Kakusan-ni|en|Kakusan-ni|qid=Q11630322|lt=Kakuzan-ni}}, later married Tokimune. Yoshikage also formed strong alliances with other prominent {{ill|Gokenin|en|Gokenin|qid=Q63765|lt=Gokenin}}, including the {{ill|Nagai clan|ja|長井氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11651463}}, {{ill|Nikaidō clan|en|Nikaidō clan|qid=Q2000952|lt=Nikaidō clan}}, and {{ill|Mutō clan|ja|武藤氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11546509}}. 
In {{ill|Kenchō|en|Kenchō|qid=Q1194270|lt=Kenchō}} 5 (1253), Yoshikage retired to a monastic life in May and passed away in June at the age of 44.
The position and influence of the Adachi clan, established by Yoshikage and his father, Kagemori, peaked during the time of his son Yasumori under Tokimune's administration.
